access_method: open HTTPS resolve, no authentication, no access-control bypass
label_semantics: numeric; label 0 = legitimate, label 1 = phishing (verified against the dataset card and by row inspection: apex domains such as higgsfield.ai carry label 0)
license_notes: Dataset card declares MIT for the compilation and the build pipeline is MIT licensed.

The legitimate class is the Tranco top-10K list. Tranco aggregates providers including Cloudflare Radar under CC BY-NC 4.0 (non-commercial) and CrUX under CC BY-SA 4.0, so the derived legitimate rows inherit at least one non-commercial upstream component.
The phishing class is dominated by Phishing.Database (MIT) with 9 PhishStats rows and 3 OpenPhish rows; OpenPhish terms are non-commercial for detection/product use.
Conclusion: the MIT card covers the compilation, not the upstream data rights. This is NOT cleared as production-compatible for a public deployment.
known_biases: Every legitimate row is constructed as http://<domain> (9973 http, 0 https), so the legitimate class is scheme-degenerate and injecting it into training would create a new HTTP-is-legitimate bias.
Legitimate rows are domains only; there are no legitimate queries and no legitimate apex-with-path rows.
Tranco ranks popularity, not safety; the publisher mitigates this by dropping any domain that later appears in a phishing feed, but the base label is still an inference.
training_use: NOT APPROVED - upstream non-commercial component (Cloudflare Radar CC BY-NC 4.0 via Tranco) and OpenPhish non-commercial terms
diagnostic_use: APPROVED FOR DIAGNOSTIC ONLY - used in docs/apex_representation_test to measure, not to train, select, or ship
